items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Function names are mostly clear (convertYuv420pToRgb, hScale8To15). But stride arithmetic like `@ptrFromInt(@as(usize, @intCast(@as(isize, @intCast(@intFromPtr(u_base))) + ...)))` is repeated inline, and constants such as mc.c24294/c48001/c165 have no FFmpeg derivation.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Everything is in one main.zig of more than 3000 lines. initFilter alone spans L152-387 (over 100 lines). swscale_process inlines the NV12/NV21 interleave and deinterleave loops with copy-pasted stride math. .zig-cache and the built zig-out .so are committed.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Allocation failures go through swscale_destroy and return null, and null handles or planes return -1. But magic constants are common (1<<14 memsets, mulhi constants), and `@intCast` on strides relies on unchecked assumptions.

items.name: Geometry, stride and tail handling
items.name_zh: 几何尺寸、步长与尾部处理
items.evidence: SIMD loops have scalar tails (`while (x < ctx.chr_dst_w)`), and every plane is addressed through its own src/dst stride. The contract passes. I could not verify NULL returns for unsupported combinations or behaviour on tiny frames.

items.name: ABI and build-target conformance
items.name_zh: ABI 与构建目标符合要求
items.evidence: nm -D was checked. The three exported functions use C linkage, swscale_process returns 0 on success, filters and buffers are precomputed in swscale_create, build.zig sets the target, and the code is single-threaded with no ff_ symbols.
